name: Estimate heights using simple geometry
blurb: Three classic methods — the shadow ratio, the stick method and the pencil method — let you measure a tree or a building to within a few percent using nothing.
gear: A sunny day for the shadow method
steps: Learn the shadow method: measure your own height and shadow, then the object’s shadow. The ratio gives the height directly.
Learn the stick method: hold a stick equal to your arm length vertically at arm’s length, walk until the stick exactly spans the object, and your distance to the object equals its height.
Learn the pencil method for scaling against a known reference such as a person standing at the base.
Learn to use your phone’s inclinometer with basic trigonometry for a more precise answer.
Practise on objects you can verify — a known building, a flagpole, a house.
Compare methods on the same object to see how they disagree.
tips: The stick method fails if the ground slopes. Choose a level line of sight.
Consistent eye height matters. Small errors there scale up over distance.
proof: You measure a tall tree three different ways and all three agree within 10%.
